_: Tier-3 wall (DECISIONS.md CR-15). Config here, never in the logic. Read at build time and emitted as data attributes - no runtime fetch.
_requireCanvas: Include a registry entry only if its page actually contains a <canvas>. This exists because /games/fulfillment/ is 'Fulfillment - Manual' - documentation with no canvas and no loop - and it was once shipped into an arcade cabinet. The build proves a game is a game rather than trusting a category field.
_requireAttract: A game appears on the wall only if it has its standalone attract asset at <game>/attract/index.html (game law 5b). A game without one is listed in the index below but shows no panel, and the build reports it by name. Never an empty box.
_order: Reading order on the wall. Anything not named here follows in registry order, so adding a game never makes it vanish.
_maxLive: Hard cap on attract screens mounted at once. Each is a real canvas loop, so this is a CPU budget. The furthest from the viewport is evicted first.
_mountMargin: How far outside the viewport a panel mounts, so it is already running when it scrolls into view rather than starting blank.
_unmountMargin: REMOVED 2026-09-08. It drove a second unmount observer, and having mount and unmount decided by two separate observers is exactly what let the two states disagree: a panel could be evicted while still on screen and never remount, because IntersectionObserver only fires on threshold crossings. wall.js now reconciles to a desired set instead, so one margin is enough.
